title: Full Platform Migration: Monolith to Microservices Architecture
summary: An extended planning session covering the complete migration strategy from a Rails monolith to a microservices architecture using Kubernetes. The team discussed service boundaries, data migration, deployment strategy, testing, monitoring, team structure, and rollback planning across a 6-month timeline.

topics.name: Service Boundary Definition
topics.insight: Identified 12 bounded contexts using Domain-Driven Design. Top candidates for extraction: User Auth, Billing, Notifications, Content Management, and Analytics.

topics.name: Database Migration Strategy
topics.insight: Each microservice gets its own PostgreSQL database. Use Change Data Capture (CDC) with Debezium during the transition period to keep monolith and service databases in sync.

topics.name: API Gateway Selection
topics.insight: Compared Kong, Traefik, and AWS API Gateway. Kong selected for its plugin ecosystem and on-premise deployment flexibility.

topics.name: Inter-Service Communication
topics.insight: Synchronous calls via gRPC for latency-critical paths. Async events via Apache Kafka for eventual consistency workflows like notifications and analytics.

topics.name: Container Orchestration
topics.insight: Kubernetes on EKS chosen over ECS for better multi-cloud portability. Helm charts for deployment configuration.

topics.name: Service Mesh
topics.insight: Istio evaluated but deferred due to operational complexity. Will start with basic Kubernetes networking and revisit when services exceed 15.

topics.name: Observability Stack
topics.insight: Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, Jaeger for distributed tracing, ELK stack for centralized logging. OpenTelemetry SDK for instrumentation.

topics.name: CI/CD Pipeline Redesign
topics.insight: Move from single monolith pipeline to per-service pipelines. GitHub Actions with shared workflow templates to reduce duplication.

topics.name: Team Topology
topics.insight: Shift from feature teams to service-owning teams. Each team owns 2-3 services with full lifecycle responsibility (you build it, you run it).

topics.name: Security Model
topics.insight: Zero-trust network model. Service-to-service authentication via mTLS. JWT tokens with short-lived access tokens (15min) and refresh token rotation.

topics.name: Data Consistency Patterns
topics.insight: Saga pattern for distributed transactions (e.g., order placement). Outbox pattern to ensure reliable event publishing from database writes.

topics.name: Rollback Strategy
topics.insight: Blue-green deployments for critical services. Canary releases with 5% traffic split for non-critical services. Feature flags via LaunchDarkly for gradual rollouts.

decisions.decision: Extract User Auth service first as the migration pilot.
decisions.reason: Auth has the clearest domain boundary and fewest cross-cutting dependencies. Success here builds confidence and establishes patterns for subsequent extractions.

decisions.decision: Use gRPC for synchronous inter-service communication instead of REST.
decisions.reason: gRPC provides strong typing via Protocol Buffers, HTTP/2 multiplexing, and ~7x better serialization performance than JSON/REST for internal APIs.

decisions.decision: Adopt Strangler Fig pattern for gradual migration.
decisions.reason: Allows running monolith and microservices simultaneously. New features built in services, existing features migrated incrementally. Zero big-bang risk.

decisions.decision: PostgreSQL per service with Debezium CDC for transition sync.
decisions.reason: Database-per-service is essential for independent deployability. Debezium provides real-time CDC without application code changes in the monolith.

decisions.decision: Defer service mesh (Istio) until service count exceeds 15.
decisions.reason: Istio adds significant operational overhead (sidecar proxies, control plane). Current scale (5-8 services in Year 1) doesn't justify the complexity.

decisions.decision: Implement Saga pattern for cross-service transactions, starting with the order flow.
decisions.reason: Distributed transactions (2PC) don't scale. Sagas with compensating transactions handle failures gracefully and align with event-driven architecture.

decisions.decision: Use OpenTelemetry as the unified instrumentation standard.
decisions.reason: Vendor-neutral, supports traces/metrics/logs, and avoids lock-in to any specific observability backend. Large ecosystem of auto-instrumentation libraries.

decisions.decision: Enforce API contracts with Protocol Buffer schemas stored in a shared schema registry.
decisions.reason: Prevents breaking changes between services. Schema registry enables automated compatibility checking in CI pipelines.

actionItems.task: Set up EKS cluster with Terraform and configure base networking
Define Protocol Buffer schemas for User Auth service API
Configure Debezium CDC connector for users table in monolith DB
Create GitHub Actions workflow template for microservice CI/CD
Extract User Auth domain code from Rails monolith into standalone Go service
Deploy Prometheus + Grafana monitoring stack on EKS
Set up Jaeger for distributed tracing and integrate with Auth service
Write migration runbook documenting rollback procedures for Auth service cutover
Set up Kong API Gateway with routing rules for Auth endpoints
Configure LaunchDarkly feature flags for Auth service traffic switching
Design team topology proposal: map engineers to service-owning squads
Research and document Kafka topic naming conventions and partition strategy
Evaluate ELK vs Loki for centralized logging and present recommendation
Create architecture decision records (ADRs) for all approved decisions
Plan load testing strategy for Auth service under projected peak traffic

openQuestions: Should we use a shared PostgreSQL cluster with logical databases or fully separate RDS instances per service?
How do we handle schema migrations across services without downtime?
What is the SLA target for inter-service gRPC calls? 50ms p99?
Should we build a shared Go library for common concerns (auth middleware, logging, tracing) or keep services fully independent?
How do we manage secrets across services — Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or sealed secrets in Kubernetes?
What is the testing strategy for Saga workflows that span multiple services?
unresolvedConflicts: Platform team wants to standardize on Go for all new services; Auth team prefers Rust for its memory safety guarantees in security-critical code.
Engineering manager advocates for gradual migration over 12 months; CTO wants the first 5 services extracted within 6 months to hit board-level milestone.
Data team wants a shared event schema registry; service teams want per-service schema autonomy to avoid cross-team coordination overhead.
